name: Second Acts: Things That Died and Came Back
description: Languages spoken again, bridges rebuilt, nations restored and old ideas reborn: the history of coming back from the dead.

checkpoints.name: Echoes of antiquity
checkpoints.note: The Ancient Olympic Games end in the 390s, but the world of Classical antiquity and the ideas of Neoplatonism remain alive. Under Charlemagne the Carolingian Renaissance copies old books and revives learning.

checkpoints.name: Learning reborn
checkpoints.note: Neo-Confucianism renews an old teaching in China, and the Renaissance and Renaissance humanism bring back the learning of Greece and Rome in Europe.

checkpoints.name: Revival as style and nation
checkpoints.note: Gothic Revival architecture and Neoclassicism bring old forms back into fashion. The Partitions of Poland erase a country, and the Meiji Restoration renews Japan. Hebrew is revived as a spoken language, the Zionist movement forms, and the Olympic Games return in Athens in 1896.

checkpoints.name: Countries and stories return
checkpoints.note: Poland returns to the map in 1918, and Israel is founded in 1948. The Manx language loses its last native speaker in 1974, but is brought back by learners. New Hollywood and The Dark Knight Returns renew popular stories.

checkpoints.name: The comeback age
checkpoints.note: Germany is reunified and Lithuania regains independence in 1990, Doctor Who returns to television in 2005, Stari Most is rebuilt in Mostar in 2004, Steve Jobs returns to Apple, and the Netscape code lives on as Firefox. Notre-Dame de Paris reopens after its fire in 2019.
